title: Modular Exponentiation
description: Given non-negative integers `base` and `exp` and a positive modulus `mod`, compute `(base^exp) % mod` using binary exponentiation. By convention `0^0 = 1`, so when `exp == 0` the result is `1 % mod`.
hints: Repeatedly square `base % mod` while shifting `exp` right by 1 bit.
Whenever the lowest bit of `exp` is `1`, multiply the running answer by the current base power modulo `mod`; initialize the answer to `1 % mod` to handle `mod == 1`.
